title: Implement deterministic SDK test harness with VCR-style recording and API contract checks
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Objective: Build a deterministic, multi-language SDK test harness that supports VCR-style recording/replay, deterministic fixture generation, and automated contract checks against Redwood API schemas. This will reduce flakiness in SDK CI, make streaming ergonomics tests reproducible, and allow contract-level guardrails before shipping SDK changes.

Scope:
- Record live interactions with Redwood staging (sensitive data scrubbed) into compact VCR-style fixtures for Python, TS, Go SDKs.
- Provide deterministic replay server (local/mockserver) that can simulate streaming chunking/latency and error modes.
- Implement contract tests that validate request/response shapes and required fields against the Redwood API catalog (OpenAPI/JSON Schema).
- Support time-freezing / deterministic timestamps and seeded randomness to ensure identical outputs for local deterministic tests.
- Integrate into GitHub Actions CI matrix (language versions, runtime flags, streaming vs non-streaming) and nightly job against staging for contract drift detection.

Design decisions and constraints:
- Use VCR-style YAML/JSON recordings with metadata (SDK version, Redwood API version, seed, scrubber-version).
- Sensitive fields must be scrubbed at record time using our standard scrubber (emails, API keys, long prompt contents). Recordings stored in an internal repo with TTL policy (90 days) and size cap.
- Replay server should be lightweight (Go binary for local dev, Node shim for TS devs) and implement: deterministic chunk boundaries, configurable per-request latency profile, and response header propagation.
- Contract checks will verify both shape and semantic constraints (required params, enums). Fail CI when contract changes are detected; allow a 'contract-ack' label flow for controlled rollouts.

Acceptance criteria:
1) SDK unit/integration tests can run entirely offline using recorded fixtures for Python/TS/Go.
2) Streaming tests reproduce exact chunk boundaries and lengths when run with same seed.
3) CI pipeline runs contract tests and fails on breaking schema changes, with a clear PR workflow to update expectations.
4) Recordings are scrubbed and stored under the golden-fixtures repo; there is a documented process to refresh recordings.

Non-goals:
- This ticket does not include on-prem/private network test harness for customer infra (follow-up).

Rollout plan:
- Alpha: local tools + example fixtures for each SDK (devs only).
- Beta: integrate into PR CI for SDK repo (non-blocking).
- GA: block merges on contract drift for SDKs and nightly contract monitor against staging.

Notes: keep files small (strip heavy prompt bodies from recordings), prefer JSONL for streaming recordings to allow line-delimited replays.
tasks: Write VCR recorder library for TS/Python/Go (common contract and per-language shim)
Implement scrubber module and enforce at record time (reuse existing redact rules)
Create deterministic replay server that simulates streaming chunking/latency
Add contract test runner that pulls OpenAPI/JSON Schema from catalog and validates recorded exchanges
Add GH Actions workflow matrix across SDK languages and node/python/go versions
Document 'refresh recordings' playbook and TTL rules in Confluence
Add example fixtures for streaming generation, embeddings, and function-calling flows
